callingConvention: An aggregate larger than one register is returned through a pointer the caller passes as the first argument; the function returns nothing.
An aggregate passed by value is copied into linear memory by the caller and arrives as a pointer.
A pointer and a size_t are both i32 on wasm32.

functions.name: add_actor
functions.doc: Add an actor to a conversation and return the integer id'ing it. The actor starts at `start_position` on the default channel, with priority 0. Ids are per conversation and are never reused, so ascending order is a stable iteration order. - `speak_as` and `listen_to` are arrays of `count` names; either may be null when its count is 0. - ActorFlags::SPECTATOR and ActorFlags::DEBUG actors are given no channel or priority. Emits an EventData::ActorAdded event on success. Returns the new actor id, or LOUDER_ACTOR_NONE if the conversation is not loaded or a pointer was null.

functions.name: answer_ask
functions.doc: Answer the ask at `index` with `verdict`. Answering marks the ask complete and moves it to the back of the cache, so indexes shift: read get_ask again after each answer. Answered asks stay readable but no longer accept answers, so a host can simply keep answering until LouderError::Missing comes back and the cache has flushed itself. Returns LouderError::Ok if the answer was recorded, or LouderError::Missing if `index` was out of range or that ask had already been answered.

functions.name: clear_config
functions.doc: Remove all speakers in the config. Returns 0 on success, or 1 if `ctx` was null. Conversations and actors are untouched, so hubs naming a now-missing speaker become public again.

functions.name: declare_name
functions.doc: Assign the id of a string. If the string was already declared, returns LOUDER_NAME_NONE and leaves the existing id alone. Otherwise a new id is assigned and returned.

functions.name: deinit_louder
functions.doc: Release a context and everything it holds. Returns LouderError::Ok on success, or LouderError::Missing if `ctx` was null. Every conversation, speaker, actor, and queued event goes with it.

functions.name: flush_events
functions.doc: Remove every queued event. The queue is indexed from 0 again afterwards, so the next get_event with index 0 reads the first event queued after this call.

functions.name: force_position
functions.doc: Move an actor to another position directly. - `fake_priority` is unused if `0`, otherwise overrides the priority of the destination. Because 0 is the ordinary default priority, this cannot force an actor's priority *to* 0 over a hub that sets one. - `fake_channel` is unused if LOUDER_NAME_NONE, otherwise overrides the channel of the destination. Returns 0 on success, or 1 if the conversation, actor, or destination was missing, or if an auto hub ran out of choices.

functions.name: force_warp
functions.doc: Move an actor to another position as if it had moved through the network. - `fake_priority` is unused if `0`, otherwise overrides the priority of the destination. Because 0 is the ordinary default priority, this cannot force an actor's priority *to* 0 over a hub that sets one. - `fake_channel` is unused if LOUDER_NAME_NONE, otherwise overrides the channel of the destination. Other actors sharing the actor's channel may be pulled along, exactly as if the actor had chosen. Returns 0 on success, or 1 if the conversation, actor, or destination was missing, or if an auto hub ran out of choices.

functions.name: get_actor_additional
functions.doc: Get an actor's additional data under `key`. Returns a zero variant if the actor does not exist or has nothing stored under `key`.

functions.name: get_actor_channel
functions.doc: Get the channel of an actor. Actors with ActorFlags::SPECTATOR or ActorFlags::DEBUG are not part of the flow and read as LOUDER_NAME_NONE.

functions.name: get_actor_flags
functions.doc: Get the flags of an actor. Returns ActorFlags::empty if the actor does not exist.

functions.name: get_actor_position
functions.doc: Get the position of an actor. Returns BLANK_POSITION if the actor does not exist.

functions.name: get_actor_priority
functions.doc: Get the priority of an actor. Actors outside the flow read as 0.

functions.name: get_ask
functions.doc: Get the ask at `index`. Asks are not in a stable order, so read them until one comes back LouderOption::None rather than assuming the queue only grows.

functions.name: get_dialogue_rules
functions.doc: Read the dialogue rules currently in effect. A fresh context has every rule on. Returns an empty set if `ctx` was null, since a null context is not running any dialogue.

functions.name: get_event
functions.doc: Get the event at `index`. Returns LouderOption::None once `index` is past the end of the queue, or if `ctx` is null. Poll from index 0 upwards until that happens, then call flush_events.

functions.name: get_hub_additional
functions.doc: Get a hub's additional data under `key`. Returns a zero variant if the hub does not exist or has nothing stored under `key`.

functions.name: get_hub_callbacks
functions.doc: Get the callbacks associated with a hub as a name. The schema stores callbacks newline separated; this returns the whole block as one name. Returns LOUDER_NAME_NONE if the hub has none.

functions.name: get_hub_channel
functions.doc: Get the channel of a hub. Returns LOUDER_NAME_NONE if the hub does not change the channel, in which case an actor keeps whatever channel it already had.

functions.name: get_hub_choice_count
functions.doc: Get the number of choices on a hub from an actor's perspective. Only choices the actor could actually take are counted, so this applies the visibility, recipient, and spoke rules. Returns 0 for an unknown hub or actor.

functions.name: get_hub_choice_link
functions.doc: Get the position a choice on a hub links to. Returns BLANK_POSITION if the choice does not exist or is not available to `actor_perspective`.

functions.name: get_hub_choice_text
functions.doc: Get the text of a choice on a hub as a name. A choice has no text of its own, so this is the text of the hub it links to. Returns LOUDER_NAME_NONE if the choice does not exist or is not available to `actor_perspective`.

functions.name: get_hub_expressions
functions.doc: Get the expressions associated with a hub as a name. The schema stores expressions newline separated; this returns the whole block as one name, so the caller splits it to get individual expressions. Returns LOUDER_NAME_NONE if the hub has none.

functions.name: get_hub_flags
functions.doc: Get the flags of a hub. Returns HubFlags::empty if the hub does not exist.

functions.name: get_hub_priority
functions.doc: Get the priority of a hub. Returns 0 if the hub does not exist, which is also the default priority.

functions.name: get_hub_speaker
functions.doc: Get the speaker of a hub. Returns LOUDER_NAME_NONE if the hub has no speaker, which means it is visible to everyone, or if the hub does not exist.

functions.name: get_hub_text
functions.doc: Get the text of a hub as a name. Returns LOUDER_NAME_NONE if the hub has no text or does not exist. Read the string back with read_name.

functions.name: get_named_id
functions.doc: Get the id of a string. Returns LOUDER_NAME_NONE if the string was never declared, or if either pointer was null. - `buffer`: the string bytes to look up. - `max_size`: the number of bytes to read from `buffer`.

functions.name: get_next_speaker_listen_to
functions.doc: Iterate the speakers that `speaker` is listening to. Pass LOUDER_NAME_NONE as `start` to begin, then pass the previous result until LOUDER_NAME_NONE comes back. Returns LOUDER_NAME_NONE for an unknown speaker.

functions.name: get_speaker_additional
functions.doc: Get a speaker's additional data under `key`. The speaker config is a singleton rather than a per-conversation object, so this takes no conversation. Returns a zero variant if the speaker is unknown or has nothing stored under `key`.

functions.name: get_speaker_flags
functions.doc: Get the flags of a speaker. A speaker that has not been declared reads as SpeakerFlags::empty, which is public by default, so a hub naming it still appears to everyone.

functions.name: get_story_state
functions.doc: Get a story state value under `state`. The variable's own name decides where it is stored: a leading underscore means it is not saved, and an uppercase first letter means it is shared across conversations. Variables that have never been written read as 0. Reading from a conversation that is not loaded also reads as 0.

functions.name: init_louder
functions.doc: Initialize the engine and return a new context. Initializes the name table, the event queue, and the ask cache. Release the returned handle with deinit_louder. Returns null only if allocation failed.

functions.name: load_conversation_config
functions.doc: Load the conversation config from a JSON document in `buffer`. - The bytes have to be UTF-8 and the error scheme is the one in load_conversation_json, with speakers as the target objects instead of hubs. - The config is a singleton as opposed to a named conversation instance, so this takes no conversation name. - Objects are speakers and their configurations. A speaker already in the config is replaced rather than treated as an error.

functions.name: load_conversation_json
functions.doc: Load a conversation from a JSON document in `buffer`. The buffer holds `max_size` bytes. JSON is text, so those bytes have to be UTF-8 for the engine to read them; LOUDER_LOAD_MALFORMED_JSON is returned if they are not, and re-encoding them is the host's job rather than the engine's. - The JSON is expected in array form; LOUDER_LOAD_NOT_A_LIST is returned otherwise. - Standard JSON syntax errors are returned as LOUDER_LOAD_MALFORMED_JSON. - Standard properties are left default or read from matching JSON fields. - Additional JSON fields are treated as additional data on hubs. - LOUDER_LOAD_ALREADY_LOADED is returned if `conversation` is already occupied by another loaded conversation. - Problems with individual records do not fail the load. They are emitted as events instead, carrying the offending hub's position in Motion::source_position and the LoadError in Motion::target_position.

functions.name: make_event_data_actor_added
functions.doc: Build an EventData::ActorAdded.

functions.name: make_event_data_actor_removed
functions.doc: Build an EventData::ActorRemoved.

functions.name: make_event_data_additional_data_change
functions.doc: Build an EventData::AdditionalDataChange.

functions.name: make_event_data_callback
functions.doc: Build an EventData::Callback, naming the callback.

functions.name: make_event_data_channel_change
functions.doc: Build an EventData::ChannelChange.

functions.name: make_event_data_choice_appearance
functions.doc: Build an EventData::ChoiceAppearance.

functions.name: make_event_data_condition
functions.doc: Build an EventData::Condition.

functions.name: make_event_data_conversation_added
functions.doc: Build an EventData::ConversationAdded, naming the conversation.

functions.name: make_event_data_conversation_removed
functions.doc: Build an EventData::ConversationRemoved, naming the conversation.

functions.name: make_event_data_force_motion
functions.doc: Build an EventData::ForceMotion.

functions.name: make_event_data_load_error
functions.doc: Build an EventData::LoadError. The engine emits these itself when it cannot read a record of a loaded document, so this exists to round out the set rather than because a host has a reason to raise one.

functions.name: make_event_data_none
functions.doc: Build the EventData::None variant, which carries nothing.

functions.name: make_event_data_regular_motion
functions.doc: Build an EventData::RegularMotion.

functions.name: make_event_data_speaker_added
functions.doc: Build an EventData::SpeakerAdded, naming the speaker.

functions.name: make_event_data_speaker_change
functions.doc: Build an EventData::SpeakerChange, naming the speaker.

functions.name: make_event_data_speaker_removed
functions.doc: Build an EventData::SpeakerRemoved, naming the speaker.

functions.name: make_event_data_statement
functions.doc: Build an EventData::Statement, naming the expression.

functions.name: make_event_data_text_change
functions.doc: Build an EventData::TextChange, naming the text.

functions.name: make_event_data_warp
functions.doc: Build an EventData::Warp.

functions.name: make_some_ask
functions.doc: Build a LouderOption::Some holding an ask.

functions.name: make_some_event
functions.doc: Build a LouderOption::Some holding an event.

functions.name: make_variant_bool
functions.doc: Build a boolean as a LouderVariant::Int of 1 or 0.

functions.name: make_variant_float
functions.doc: Build a LouderVariant::Float.

functions.name: make_variant_int
functions.doc: Build a LouderVariant::Int.

functions.name: make_variant_string
functions.doc: Build a LouderVariant::String, naming the string rather than carrying it.

functions.name: make_variant_zero
functions.doc: Build the LouderVariant::Int of 0 that an unwritten variable reads as.

functions.name: next_actor_from_flags
functions.doc: Iterate the actors matching certain flags. With `exact` nonzero the flags must match exactly; otherwise every bit in `include` must be present. Pass LOUDER_ACTOR_NONE as `start` to begin.

functions.name: next_actor_in_channel
functions.doc: Iterate the actors in a channel. Pass LOUDER_ACTOR_NONE as `start` to begin. Actors outside the flow have no channel and are never returned.

functions.name: next_actor_in_channel_and_position
functions.doc: Iterate the actors in a channel at a specific position. Pass LOUDER_ACTOR_NONE as `start` to begin.

functions.name: next_actor_listening
functions.doc: Iterate the speakers an actor listens to. Includes the actor's `listen_to` speakers plus the listening speakers of the speakers it speaks as. Pass LOUDER_NAME_NONE as `start` to begin.

functions.name: next_actor_listening_base
functions.doc: Iterate the base speakers an actor listens to. These are the actor's own `listen_to` speakers, without the ones reachable through who it speaks as. See next_actor_listening for the wider set.

functions.name: next_actor_listening_to
functions.doc: Iterate the actors listening to a speaker. This covers `listen_to` plus the listening actors derived from the listening speakers of the speakers an actor speaks as. Pass LOUDER_ACTOR_NONE as `start` to begin.

functions.name: next_actor_speak_as
functions.doc: Iterate the speakers an actor speaks as. Pass LOUDER_NAME_NONE as `start` to begin, then pass the previous result until LOUDER_NAME_NONE comes back.

functions.name: next_actor_speaking_as
functions.doc: Iterate the actors speaking as a speaker. Pass LOUDER_ACTOR_NONE as `start` to begin.

functions.name: next_hub_by_channel
functions.doc: Iterate the hubs in a channel. Hubs that name no channel belong to the default channel, so searching for it also finds them. Pass BLANK_POSITION as `start` to begin.

functions.name: next_hub_by_priority
functions.doc: Iterate the hubs with a priority within `[priority_min, priority_max]`. The bounds are inclusive. Pass BLANK_POSITION as `start` to begin.

functions.name: next_hub_from_flags
functions.doc: Iterate the hubs matching certain flags. With `exact` nonzero the flags must match exactly; otherwise every bit in `include` must be present. Pass BLANK_POSITION as `start` to begin.

functions.name: next_hub_from_tags
functions.doc: Iterate the hubs containing all, or exactly, the given tags. With `exact` nonzero the hub must carry exactly the listed tags; otherwise carrying extra tags is fine. Pass BLANK_POSITION as `start` to begin.

functions.name: next_hub_heard_by
functions.doc: Iterate the hubs heard by a speaker. This searches the speaker's own listening speakers as well as the speaker itself, which are the hubs that may appear to an actor speaking as this speaker. Pass BLANK_POSITION as `start` to begin.

functions.name: next_hub_recipient
functions.doc: Iterate the recipients of a hub. Returns LOUDER_NAME_NONE when the hub has no recipients, which means the hub is not restricted. Pass LOUDER_NAME_NONE as `start` to begin.

functions.name: next_hub_spoken_by
functions.doc: Iterate the hubs spoken by a speaker. Pass BLANK_POSITION as `start` to begin.

functions.name: next_hub_tag
functions.doc: Iterate the tags of a position. Pass LOUDER_NAME_NONE as `start` to begin.

functions.name: push_ask
functions.doc: Push an ask onto the ask cache, used for testing. Returns LouderError::Ok on success, or LouderError::Missing if either pointer was null.

functions.name: read_name
functions.doc: Read the bytes associated with an id into `buffer`. The bytes come back exactly as they went in, so a name declared in some encoding is read in that same one. Decoding them is the host's job, since the engine never displays anything itself. Writes 0 bytes and a terminator if no name is associated with the id, or if either pointer was null. Returns the number of bytes written, excluding the terminator.

functions.name: read_snapshot_json
functions.doc: Serialize the story state, along with the positions and details of every actor, in JSON into `buffer`. The document has a `state` object and an `actors` array, both ordered so that the output is reproducible. The document is written as UTF-8. Returns the number of bytes written excluding the terminator; a negative value means the conversation is not loaded.

functions.name: read_state_json
functions.doc: Serialize the story state in JSON into `buffer`. Every bucket is included: the conversation's own saved and unsaved variables, and the shared ones. Keys are written in ascending id order so the output is reproducible. The document is written as UTF-8. Returns the number of bytes written excluding the terminator; a negative value means the conversation is not loaded.

functions.name: remove_actor
functions.doc: Remove an actor from a conversation. Returns 0 on success, or 1 if the actor or conversation did not exist. Emits an EventData::ActorRemoved event on success.

functions.name: remove_conversation
functions.doc: Remove a conversation and all associated actors. Returns 0 on success, or 1 if the conversation was not loaded. Shared story state is kept, since it outlives any one conversation.

functions.name: select_choice
functions.doc: Select a choice on an actor's current hub. The choice must be one the actor could actually take; see get_hub_choice_count for what that means. Auto hubs along the way are resolved by taking the first choice available at each one. Returns 0 on success, or 1 if the actor, hub, or choice was missing, if the choice is not available to this actor, or if an auto hub ran out of choices.

functions.name: set_dialogue_rules
functions.doc: Replace the dialogue rules. A rule takes effect on the next move rather than being applied to the conversation as it stands, so a host can turn one off while an actor is standing on a hub it would otherwise resolve through. Bits outside DialogueRules are ignored rather than refused, so a host carrying a configuration written for a newer engine still gets the rules this build knows about.

functions.name: set_story_state
functions.doc: Set a story state value. The variable's own name decides where it is stored, as in get_story_state. Doing nothing if `ctx` is null.

functions.name: test_push_event
functions.doc: Push an event onto the event queue, used for testing. The caller fills in the event themselves, so nothing about `code` is interpreted here. Returns LouderError::Ok on success, or LouderError::Missing if either pointer was null.
